title: Advanced Algebra Proof & Peer-Review Workflow
description: Constructs a proof for a submitted theorem, runs an independent step-by-step verification, loops revision-and-reverification until every step is valid (or a cap is hit), then gates publication behind a human mathematician's sign-off.
yaml:
apiVersion: ladder.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Workflow
metadata:
  name: advanced-algebra-proof-peer-review-workflow
  title: Advanced Algebra Proof & Peer-Review Workflow
  description: Constructs a proof for a submitted theorem, runs an independent step-by-step
    verification, loops revision-and-reverification until every step is valid (or a cap is hit),
    then gates publication behind a human mathematician's sign-off.
  version: 1.0.0
spec:
  objective: "Constructs a proof for a submitted theorem, runs an independent step-by-step
    verification, loops revision-and-reverification until every step is valid (or a cap is hit),
    then gates publication behind a human mathematician's sign-off. Trigger: user submits a theorem
    statement (with an optional draft proof sketch)"
  policies:
    maxConcurrency: 4
    onFailure: stop
    requireApprovalFor:
      - n6
  nodes:
    - id: n1
      kind: input
      name: Theorem & Proof Sketch Intake
      summary: Theorem & Proof Sketch Intake
      inputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - text
        properties:
          text:
            type: string
            description: The user's objective, source text, or instructions.
          workflowFields:
            type: object
            required:
              - theorem_statement
              - proof_sketch_optional
            properties:
              theorem_statement: {}
              proof_sketch_optional: {}
        x-ladder-input-mode: text
    - id: n2
      kind: agent
      templateRef: math-alg-01
      name: Construct/Complete Proof
      summary: Construct/Complete Proof
      role: PhD-level algebraist covering linear algebra, abstract algebra (groups/rings/fields), and
        polynomial systems.
      prompt: You are an Advanced Algebra Specialist agent. You work with vector spaces, linear
        transformations and eigen-decompositions, and abstract structures (groups, rings, fields) as
        well as systems of polynomial equations. When constructing or completing a proof, you use
        standard techniques (induction, contradiction, structural/ homomorphism arguments) and
        explicitly state which axiom or prior theorem each step relies on, so a reader can verify
        the proof against the definitions rather than trusting it on authority. You distinguish a
        result that holds generally from one that depends on a special case (finite-dimensional,
        commutative, characteristic zero, etc.) and say so explicitly rather than silently assuming
        it.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - domain-analysis
          - quantitative-analysis
          - image-understanding
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n3
      kind: agent
      templateRef: math-gen-01
      name: Verify Proof Step-by-Step
      summary: Verify Proof Step-by-Step
      role: Formal-logic-trained mathematician who checks proof validity independent of who or what
        constructed the proof.
      prompt: You are a Proof Verifier / Logic Checker agent. You check each step of a submitted proof for
        logical validity — does it actually follow from the prior steps and the stated axioms or
        theorems, or is there a gap. You flag unjustified leaps, circular reasoning, and quantifier
        errors (e.g., swapping "for all" and "there exists"), and you distinguish a proof that is
        merely incomplete (a missing case in a case analysis, an unaddressed edge case) from one
        that contains an actually false step, since the fix required is different. You verify proofs
        on their own logical merits regardless of whether they were produced by a human or another
        agent.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - domain-analysis
          - data-quality-analysis
          - image-understanding
          - quantitative-analysis
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors:
          - mcp:daw
          - mcp:proof-assistant
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n4
      kind: evaluate
      inlineRole: true
      name: Rigor Score
      summary: Evaluate fraction of steps justified.
      role: Deterministic metric evaluator
      prompt: Evaluate the upstream result using fraction of steps justified. Return a score, pass/fail
        verdict, evidence, uncertainty, and the smallest corrective action. Do not claim
        programmatic measurement unless the host supplies the required tool.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - evaluation
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - score
          - passed
          - reasons
        properties:
          score:
            type: number
          passed:
            type: boolean
          reasons:
            type: array
            items:
              type: string
      config:
        threshold: 0.8
    - id: n5
      kind: condition
      name: All Steps Valid
      summary: All Steps Valid
      config:
        expression: verification_report.all_valid == true
        branches:
          - label: "True"
            when: "true"
          - label: "False"
            when: "false"
    - id: n7
      kind: agent
      templateRef: math-alg-01
      name: Revise Proof Using Verifier Feedback
      summary: Revise Proof Using Verifier Feedback
      role: PhD-level algebraist covering linear algebra, abstract algebra (groups/rings/fields), and
        polynomial systems.
      prompt: You are an Advanced Algebra Specialist agent. You work with vector spaces, linear
        transformations and eigen-decompositions, and abstract structures (groups, rings, fields) as
        well as systems of polynomial equations. When constructing or completing a proof, you use
        standard techniques (induction, contradiction, structural/ homomorphism arguments) and
        explicitly state which axiom or prior theorem each step relies on, so a reader can verify
        the proof against the definitions rather than trusting it on authority. You distinguish a
        result that holds generally from one that depends on a special case (finite-dimensional,
        commutative, characteristic zero, etc.) and say so explicitly rather than silently assuming
        it.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - domain-analysis
          - quantitative-analysis
          - image-understanding
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n_loop3
      kind: loop
      name: Revise Until Valid
      summary: Repeat a bounded revision sequence until verification_report.all_valid == true.
      config:
        body:
          - n3
          - n4
          - n5
          - n7
        exitCondition: verification_report.all_valid == true
        maxIterations: 6
        onExhausted: stop
    - id: n6
      kind: approval
      name: Mathematician Sign-off Before Publication
      summary: Pause for reviewing mathematician; on timeout, escalate.
    - id: n8
      kind: agent
      templateRef: math-gen-01
      name: Final Formatted Write-up (LaTeX)
      summary: Final Formatted Write-up (LaTeX)
      role: Formal-logic-trained mathematician who checks proof validity independent of who or what
        constructed the proof.
      prompt: You are a Proof Verifier / Logic Checker agent. You check each step of a submitted proof for
        logical validity — does it actually follow from the prior steps and the stated axioms or
        theorems, or is there a gap. You flag unjustified leaps, circular reasoning, and quantifier
        errors (e.g., swapping "for all" and "there exists"), and you distinguish a proof that is
        merely incomplete (a missing case in a case analysis, an unaddressed edge case) from one
        that contains an actually false step, since the fix required is different. You verify proofs
        on their own logical merits regardless of whether they were produced by a human or another
        agent.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - domain-analysis
          - data-quality-analysis
          - image-understanding
          - quantitative-analysis
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors:
          - mcp:daw
          - mcp:proof-assistant
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: workflow-output
      kind: output
      name: Validated result
      summary: Return the completed advanced algebra proof & peer-review workflow deliverable, validation
        evidence, and unresolved uncertainty.
  edges:
    - id: wf-math-03-edge-1
      from: n1
      to: n2
      kind: data
    - id: wf-math-03-edge-2
      from: n2
      to: n3
      kind: data
    - id: wf-math-03-edge-3
      from: n3
      to: n4
      kind: data
    - id: wf-math-03-edge-4
      from: n4
      to: n5
      kind: data
    - id: wf-math-03-edge-5
      from: n5
      to: n6
      kind: control
      condition: "true"
    - id: wf-math-03-edge-6
      from: n5
      to: n_loop3
      kind: control
      condition: "false"
    - id: wf-math-03-edge-7
      from: n_loop3
      to: n6
      kind: control
      condition: loop_exit
    - id: wf-math-03-edge-8
      from: n6
      to: n8
      kind: control
      condition: approved
    - id: wf-math-03-output-1
      from: n7
      to: workflow-output
      kind: dependency
    - id: wf-math-03-output-2
      from: n8
      to: workflow-output
      kind: dependency
